system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. Property-only voice, music-style, beat and sound-texture references condition a new sound; they do not play the original recording. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.

fragments.shot:shot-1:description: The complete vertical character-reference sheet remains present in its original layout: the large rainy hero panel at top, the FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, and BACK turnaround row in the middle, and the FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, and BOOTS detail row at the bottom. Inside the hero panel, fine rain streaks begin to drift diagonally through the cool blue-gray night, and warm amber reflections shiver across the wet pavement, metal railings, and illuminated building. The man in the black high-collared tactical jacket holds his three-quarter stance while the jacket hem and small topknot stir faintly. The turnaround and detail panels keep their plain charcoal backdrops and quiet held poses, with existing borders and labels fixed in place. The motion starts as a gentle, continuous drift that leaves the sheet's composition intact.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:0: The complete reference sheet is held in its supplied arrangement, all panels and labels intact.

fragments.shot:shot-1:event:2: Rain streaks drift diagonally and wet reflections waver in the hero panel.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:3: A subtle water ripple supports the drifting motion.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:4: The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.shot:shot-2:description: The rain in the hero panel thickens into finer, faster drifting streaks, and puddles ripple under shifting warm amber and cool blue-gray reflections. The wet metal railings and distant city lights shimmer as the downpour combs across the scene, while the man's dark jacket and gathered hair move only subtly with his steady breathing. In the turnaround row, the front, profile, and back views retain their arms-at-the-sides poses with the faintest rise and fall; the studio backdrops stay clean, still, and evenly shadowed. Every panel, border, and existing label remains fully visible and locked to its place as the sheet's internal weather grows more active. The detail crops keep their close, quiet studies of face, collar, hands, and boots.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:0: Rain intensifies slightly with soft water ripples.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:1: Puddles catch shifting amber and blue-gray reflections.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:2: The turnaround figures breathe subtly while holding their poses.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:3: Faint fabric movement accompanies the steady rain.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:4: The camera holds a static shot.
fragments.shot:shot-3:description: The drifting rain eases into a last scatter of drops, and the wet reflections settle back toward stillness in the hero panel. The man's jacket and hair come to rest in the original three-quarter stance, and the front, side, back, face, collar, hands, and boots studies return to their quiet held poses. Residual droplets slide from the railings, faint ripples fade across the pavement, and the warm amber and cool blue-gray highlights soften without changing the sheet's layout. The full reference sheet remains visible, with all panels, borders, and existing labels intact as the motion calms to a gentle close. The final stillness preserves the complete supplied image.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:0: Rain fades to a light patter.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:2: Jacket hem and topknot come to rest.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:4: The camera pulls out with small amplitude at slow speed.

facts.text: The image is a vertical multi-panel character reference sheet: a large cinematic hero image at the top, a row of three full-body turnaround views in the middle, and a row of four detail crops at the bottom.

In the top hero panel, a person stands on wet, reflective pavement at night as rain falls, with metal railings on both sides, city lights in the distance, and an illuminated building facade to the right.
The person wears a black high-collared tactical jacket with a chest strap and buckle, a dark shirt, black cargo pants, and black lace-up combat boots.
The person has short dark hair that is shaved at the sides, with longer hair gathered into a small topknot or bun at the back.
The middle row contains three full-body studio views against a dark gray backdrop, labeled FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, and BACK; the figure stands with arms at the sides in each.
The bottom row contains four labeled detail panels: FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, and BOOTS.
The FACE close-up shows a neutral, stern expression, visible skin texture, and a scar near the eyebrow on the viewer's left.
The JACKET COLLAR detail shows black fabric with straps and metal buckles; the HANDS detail shows weathered, visibly soiled hands; the BOOTS detail shows worn black leather lace-up combat boots.

Lighting is low-key and moody: the hero panel uses cool blue-gray night tones with warm amber street and window lights, while the turnaround and detail panels use soft directional light against charcoal backgrounds.
Visible on-screen text reads HERO, FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, BACK, FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, and BOOTS.

limitations: Small background signage or markings in the upper-right building area are not clearly legible.
